notes: Fourth consecutive day of the four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security), each briefed with the manifest, prior run logs, and the relevant slice of already-filed entries in data/events/ so budget went to fresh ground. All direct WebFetch attempts hit the expected EGRESS_BLOCKED; every filed entry rests on a search result quoting or citing an organisation's own page, or clearly-labeled secondary reporting where noted. Genuinely thin for fresh yesterday/today announcements after three dense prior days -- most new value came from forward-dated OpenAI API deprecations, hardware/silicon disclosures (Arm CSS for Mobile 2, ASML/TSMC and Intel/ASML High-NA EUV milestones), an FTC-Amazon trial reschedule, a GitHub Actions runner deprecation, an AWS Lambda runtime EOS date, a tied-together CISA KEV deadline for this week's Patch-Tuesday zero-days, and five corrections tightening dates/confidence on entries already on file (GPT-6 Astra's system-card safety detail, JDK 27 and GitHub Universe 2026 upgraded to confirmed on sources already used, PostgreSQL 19 corrected off a stale 'expected September' date to reflect it's still in beta, and Patch Tuesday's summary filled in with the two zero-day CVE numbers). Two significant EU AI Act deadlines from the Digital Omnibus regulation (Annex III high-risk obligations postponed to 2027-12-02; Annex I embedded high-risk obligations to 2028-08-02) fall outside the 12-month write window and were deliberately left as entries -- noting them here per the rule so they aren't lost, to be picked up when the window reaches them. The recurring 'xAI Grok 4.7 ~Sept 12' lead was re-chased and dropped again for resting only on low-credibility aggregator interpretation of a tweet, consistent with the 09-06 run's finding.
concerns: The Amazon Bedrock AI21 Jamba 1.5 / TwelveLabs Marengo Embed 2.7 retirement entry (filed 2026-09-07, confidence 'expected') is still sourced only to a secondary tracker (vorplabs.com) after a second day of trying -- WebFetch to docs.aws.amazon.com's own model-lifecycle pages is consistently EGRESS_BLOCKED and no search result has surfaced AWS's own page text for this specific date. Worth a maintainer checking the AWS console/API directly rather than search if this needs firming to 'confirmed'.

Aggregator sites covering this week's Microsoft Patch Tuesday give inconsistent specific CVE numbers for the same 'critical Exchange/SharePoint' claims (e.g. CVE-2026-62911 vs CVE-2026-55007 for Exchange; two different SharePoint CVE pairs), with no two independent outlets agreeing on any single number -- left unfiled rather than picking one arbitrarily. Only the two zero-day CVEs actually added to CISA's KEV catalog (CVE-2026-81963, CVE-2026-85880) had 3+ independent sources agreeing, and those are what got filed.
